# twenty_workspace_member

Manages access for one email in the authenticated workspace. Create sends an invitation without waiting for acceptance and never adopts existing access. See [required permissions](../guides/authentication.md#permissions).

## Example usage

```terraform
data "twenty_role" "member" {
  label = "Member"
}

# Keep the operator and recovery administrator out of this set.
resource "twenty_workspace_member" "declared" {
  for_each = toset(["alice@example.com", "bob@example.com"])
  email    = each.key
  role_id  = data.twenty_role.member.id
}
```

## Lifecycle

Acceptance changes status from `pending` to `accepted` without changing the `workspaceUUID/email` ID. Pending role changes revoke and reissue the invitation, invalidating the old link. Accepted role changes reassign the member's role. An `expired` invitation needs replacement; review the plan before applying. Refresh never resends mail.

Changing the email replaces access. Removing a `for_each` entry removes that email's access; undeclared memberships are untouched. Accepted-member removal can also transfer or delete data. Read the [membership guide](../guides/membership.md) before removal or recovery from a failed operation.

Built-in roles can be assigned even when their definitions are protected. Use managed-role references for Terraform ordering. Invitations that reference a custom role still block its deletion, including expired invitations and invitations outside Terraform.

The operator cannot be managed. Changes must preserve the last workspace member and an independent full-settings administrator.

## Import

Write matching configuration first. Import using the lowercase workspace UUID and email, separated by `/`. Get the workspace UUID from [twenty_workspace](../data-sources/workspace.md); it must match the provider. Member and invitation UUIDs are not import IDs.

```shell
# Replace the workspace UUID and mailbox. Use the same authenticated workspace.
terraform import 'twenty_workspace_member.declared["alice@example.com"]' '77777777-7777-4777-8777-777777777777/alice@example.com'
```

Import reads the current role without changing it. Match that role in configuration; a later apply with a different `role_id` changes it. Invitations without an explicit role use the current workspace default.

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `email` (String) One bare ASCII email address, explicitly lowercase with no surrounding spaces. Changing it replaces access.
- `role_id` (String) Lowercase, nonzero UUID of a user-assignable role in this workspace.

### Read-Only

- `expires_at` (String) Invitation expiration in RFC3339 format, otherwise null. Expired invitations do not count as active desired access.
- `id` (String) Stable identity and import format: lowercase workspace UUID/email. Remains unchanged when an invitation is accepted.
- `invitation_id` (String) Native invitation UUID while pending or expired, otherwise null. No invitation token or link is stored.
- `member_id` (String) Workspace-member UUID after acceptance, otherwise null. Not the global user or user-workspace ID.
- `ownership_confirmed` (Boolean) Whether Terraform may change this access. False after an ambiguous send, external replacement, or unverified access after cancellation. Inspect and explicitly import remaining access before further changes; refresh alone cannot confirm ownership.
- `status` (String) pending, accepted, or expired on successful reads. Expired invitations need replacement; refresh never resends mail. unconfirmed or absent can remain after a failed mutation until refresh determines remaining access.
- `workspace_id` (String) Authenticated workspace UUID. This is not a selector.
